# Design

Five waves. Wave 1 builds sixteen parts with disjoint paths so they run in parallel: the attestor's share store, its secp256k1 and Ed25519 signing wrappers, its dealer import and refresh, its peer transport, its chain-side and kernel-side decoders and policy, its authentication and audit; the import of the gateway, SDK and demo into human/wallet as one workspace and of the app into human/apps/wallet with every secret scrubbed; the gates under tools/wallet; the deployment definitions; and three kernel-side repairs the wallet depends on - the identity provider accepting the wallet's identity assertion, the human service executing a submitted plan instead of echoing it, and the hosted endpoint degrading honestly when the kernel is unreachable. Wave 2 assembles: the attestor daemon with its API and a five-node in-process end-to-end test; the gateway's keyless signing core, nonce store and RPC pool; the removal of the funded lane and the agent consent repair; the SDK provider and its Paxeer X and LayerX modules; the ceremony tool; the app's removal of every non-embedded surface; and the kernel-side signing policy. Wave 3 integrates against real processes: unified account provisioning, gateway-to-attestor tests that spawn the daemon, the rehearsal pipeline, the human service's attestor-backed custody, the attestor network and the hosted endpoint deployed, the app on the SDK provider, and the agent lane helpers. Wave 4 completes: the gateway deployed in shadow beside the old service with a fresh end-to-end account on the chain, the app's unified account and Paxeer X surfaces, release engineering, the human service end to end, runbooks and the operator checklist, the load test and the security review. Wave 5 runs the merged gate and the rehearsal against the restored copy once each and records what ran. The attestor API contract in [decision] attestor_api is fixed before wave 1 so the Go daemon, the TypeScript gateway and the Rust custody adapter code to the same shapes; wave 2 writes the schema file and golden vectors from the implementation and every later client test decodes those vectors.
